title: Codex session cannot recover from an empty or unreadable thread rollout after a TermAl restart: every turn fails on thread/resume
outcome:
OBSERVED by Greg 2026-09-11 after restarting TermAl at ~21:12Z because Codex had hung. Session session-5280 (Questly::Codex, project questly) shows "Turn failed: failed to read thread: thread-store internal error: failed to read session metadata <codex-home>/shared-app-server/sessions/2026/09/11/rollout-2026-09-11T14-11-47-01a0924f-f16b-71d0-9b55-629e76503f15.jsonl: rollout at ... is empty".

COORDINATOR FINDINGS (read-only, 21:14-21:20Z):
- The rollout file exists at C:\Users\grzeg\.termal\codex-home\shared-app-server\sessions\2026\09\11\ and is 0 bytes, mtime 21:12:15Z; it is the only empty rollout of 38 created today. The thread was created at 21:11:47Z and the app-server was killed by the restart (cargo run restarted 21:12:18Z, new server 21:13:37Z) before the rollout was written.
- The error text is the Codex app-server thread store's (not in TermAl source); TermAl surfaces it as "Turn failed" (src/messages.rs:845). On each new turn TermAl chooses thread/resume when the session has a resume_thread_id (src/codex.rs:1209, src/turns.rs:171) and there is no fallback to thread/start when resume fails, and no session action that assigns a fresh thread: the session is stuck on every turn until the persisted external thread id is replaced.
- Shared CODEX_HOME at ~/.termal/codex-home/shared-app-server is by design (docs/features/shared-codex-app-server.md:56).

ASK: when thread/resume fails with a thread-store read error (empty or unreadable rollout, missing metadata), treat the thread as lost: keep the TermAl transcript, clear the external thread id, start a fresh thread with the session's recovery instructions, and record a transcript notice naming the lost thread id. Optionally expose an explicit "new thread" session action for operators. Regression: fixture app-server returning the thread-store error on resume, then a turn succeeds on a new thread. Related: tm-vjr (phantom shells after restart).
